title: Opposition leaders reject 'third force' talk as Gachagua promises Mt Kenya direction before Christmas
key_points: Matiang'i, Nyoro and Karua told a Kirinyaga church on Sunday that the opposition is one team.
They said the opposition will field one presidential candidate, but gave no date or method.
In Embu, Gachagua said he will give Mt Kenya its political direction before Christmas.
Gachagua also asked the IEBC to say when the voter register will be audited.
content:
NAIROBI — Three opposition leaders used a church service in Kirinyaga on Sunday, November 22, to deny reports that they are building a separate "third force" inside the opposition.

At the same time, in neighbouring Embu County, former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua held his own church meeting and set out his plans for the Mt Kenya vote.

What happened in Kirinyaga

Jubilee Party leader Fred Matiang'i, People's Party of Kenya (PPK) leader Ndindi Nyoro and People's Liberation Party (PLP) leader Martha Karua attended a service at Kimunye ACK Church, The Star reported. Kirinyaga is Ms Karua's home county. MPs Anthony Kibagendi (Kitutu South), Clive Gisairo (Kitutu Masaba) and Patrick Osero (Borabu) were also there.

The four leaders, together with Siaya Governor James Orengo, have toured several regions together in recent weeks, including Gusii. The Nation reported that this had fuelled talk of a new power bloc that could shape who the opposition picks as its presidential candidate.

The leaders said that is not true:

  • Nyoro said, according to The Star: "There is only one force in the Opposition." He said the opposition will pick one flagbearer, and that leaders missing from Kirinyaga were meeting supporters in Embu and other places.
  • Matiang'i said the opposition has no time for fighting and accused unnamed people of trying to divide it for their own gain. "We have one team in Kenya in the opposition," he said, as quoted by The Kenya Times.
  • Karua said the leaders' different tours are planned together to win support across the country, and that the opposition will settle on one candidate to face President William Ruto.

According to The Kenya Times, Ms Karua has also said she is ready to step aside and back either Matiang'i or Nyoro if the opposition chooses one of them. The opposition has not yet said how or when it will pick its candidate.

What Gachagua said in Embu

Mr Gachagua, who leads the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), spoke at Wonders of God Church in Karurumo, Runyenjes, People Daily reported. He said:

  • he will give the Mt Kenya region its political direction before Christmas, after months of meetings with residents. The Kenya Times reported the dates as December 22 or 23;
  • families can use the holidays to discuss and agree on the region's preferred candidates;
  • the IEBC should say when it will audit the voter register, and remove dead voters and foreigners he claims are on it. People Daily noted he did not give evidence for the claim about foreigners.

Citizen Digital reported that Mr Gachagua also said opposition leaders now hold key voting regions, naming Mt Kenya for himself, Kisii for Matiang'i and Lower Eastern for Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka.

Why it matters

Kenya's next general election is in August 2027. The opposition has many leaders who want to run for president, and every one of them says the group will back a single candidate. How they choose that person is the big question for the coming months.

The IEBC had not publicly responded to Mr Gachagua's demands by the time of writing.
